Working notes — days 1–10

Demand: last 9 days = 8,5,4,1,7,1,7,7,0. Average ~4.4/day, max 8, lumpy. Treat demand as 0–8, plan for several high days.

Lead time: orders placed today arrive after about 2 days (confirmed by arrival columns). Inbound stock already scheduled should count toward coverage.

Costs: holding cheap ($0.10/unit/day), ordering cheap ($0.50/order), stockouts very costly. Earlier zero-order decisions caused stockouts (Day4, Day6, Day8) and high cost. Avoid stockouts; small frequent orders are fine.

Useful policy:
- Track inventory position = on hand + inbound arrivals + on-order.
- Target roughly 12–16 units of position when uncertain.
- If position drops below ~8, order enough to bring it back near 14.
- Do not order if enough inbound is already due in the next 2 days.
- When stock is 0 and high demand is likely, order immediately; waiting causes stockout cost.

Ops notes seen (forklift certification, new temp, cycle count, carrier pickup) have not changed demand or lead time. Ignore them for order quantity unless they explicitly signal a logistics change.

Current state after Day10: stock 0, 11 arriving tomorrow, 9 ordered today. Next review: after tomorrow’s arrival, check position and recent sales. If position falls below ~8, order up to ~14.

Working notes — days 1–20

Demand: lumpy 0–9/day; recent average ~4.5, but spikes to 9. Many zero-sales days are sellouts, not true low demand. Plan for high days.

Lead time: orders arrive after ~2 days. Scheduled inbound often did not prevent same/next-day stockouts.

Costs: holding cheap ($0.10/unit/day), ordering cheap ($0.50/order), stockouts very costly. Undersupply caused most losses; holding extra is acceptable.

Policy:
- Track inventory position = on hand + inbound arriving in next 2 days + on-order.
- Target position ~20–24 when uncertain, not 12–16.
- If position drops below ~16, order up to ~22.
- If stock on hand is 0–2, order immediately even if inbound is due; do not wait to see if it covers.
- Do not rely on next 2 days’ inbound alone. Order enough to cover beyond known arrivals, especially around weekends/spikes.
- Small frequent orders are fine, but quantities must be larger than recent underorders.

Ops notes (counts, cycle count, temp, carrier, forklift) have not changed demand or lead time. Ignore unless logistics changes.

Current after Day20: stock 0; inbound [7,11]; position = 18. Given repeated stockouts at similar positions, order ~4–6 to bring position toward 22. Review daily; if position <16 or stock 0, order up to ~22.

Working notes — days 1–30

Demand: lumpy 0–11/day; recent 14-day avg ~7.5, frequent 7–9, spikes 11. Zero-sales days are usually sellouts, not low demand. Plan for high demand.

Lead time: orders arrive after ~2 days. Scheduled inbound often fails to prevent same/next-day stockouts.

Costs: holding cheap ($0.10/unit/day), ordering cheap ($0.50/order), stockouts very costly. Undersupply causes most losses; extra inventory is acceptable.

Policy:
- Track inventory position = on hand + inbound next 2 days + on-order.
- Target position ~32–36 when uncertain or stock is low, not 20–24. Earlier target of ~22 was too low.
- If position <25, order up to ~34.
- If stock on hand is 0–3, order immediately and larger (e.g., ~20+), even if inbound is due. Do not wait to see if it covers.
- Do not rely on next 2 days’ inbound alone. Cover beyond known arrivals, especially around weekends/spikes.
- Small frequent orders are fine only if quantities keep position near 34; recent underorders caused repeated stockouts.
- Review daily. Raise reorder targets after any 9–11 sales day or zero-stock day.

Ops notes (temp, cycle count, forklift, racking, carrier) have not changed demand or lead time. Ignore unless logistics changes.

Current after Day30: stock 0; inbound [6,7] plus 11 pending. Position ~24, still below target. Order toward ~34 tomorrow unless large inbound arrives early.

Working notes — days 1–40

Demand: lumpy but softer. Recent 14-day avg ~4.6, range 0–9; no 11 recently. Zero-sales can be true low demand when stock is available (Day38), not just sellout. Plan for moderate demand unless spikes return.

Lead time: orders arrive after ~2 days. Scheduled inbound can fail to prevent stockouts, but recent inbound was adequate.

Costs: holding $0.10/unit/day, ordering $0.50/order. Stockouts costly but none Days31–40. Holding now dominates: maintaining position ~32–38 cost $1–3.3/day. Extra inventory is not free.

Policy:
- Track position = on hand + inbound next 2 days + on-order.
- Target ~26–30 when uncertain or low stock; use ~32–36 only if spikes/stockouts return. Earlier 32–36 was too high for recent demand; older ~22 was too low.
- If position <24, order up to ~28–30.
- If stock 0–3, order immediately enough to cover lead time + safety, but don’t automatically order 20+ if inbound is already large.
- If position >=30 and no weekend/spike risk, order 0.
- Small orders only when below target; avoid ordering just to maintain 34.
- Review daily. Raise target after 9+ sales day or stockout; lower after sustained low demand.

Ops notes (carrier pickup, temp, forklift, racking, cycle count) did not affect demand, lead time, or outcomes. Ignore unless logistics changes.

After Day40: stock 30, inbound [0,0], position 30, recent demand ~5/day. No order needed unless weekend/spike concern; 30 covers ~6 days.
